_comment: Which staged Windows PE files are Lightning's own work and which are
redistributed upstream binaries. Enforced by scripts/verify-windows-metadata.py
during packaging; the human-readable companion is docs/windows-signing-inventory.md
Only paths under lightning_owned may ever be signed with a Lightning
certificate. Everything matched by upstream_patterns ships exactly as its
project built it and is never re-signed or re-labelled as Lightning.
Operating-system libraries are not listed at all: they are never
redistributed (see the SYSTEM_DLLS set in scripts/stage-windows-runtime.py)
and are resolved from Windows itself.
A newly bundled DLL that matches nothing here is reported as UNCLASSIFIED
so a human classifies it. That is a warning rather than a build failure
on purpose: the dependency walk legitimately picks up new upstream
libraries, and breaking a release over one would be worse than surfacing
it. The rules that DO fail the build are the ones that matter for signing:
Lightning-owned metadata must match the release exactly, no non-owned
binary may claim ProductName=Lightning, and every declared Lightning-owned
file must actually be present. Only lightning_owned is ever signed, so an
unclassified file is never signed by accident.

upstream_notes.plugins/*/*.dll: Qt platform, imageformat, multimedia, TLS, SQL, style and icon-engine plugins
upstream_notes.av*.dll, sw*.dll: FFmpeg runtime behind Qt Multimedia's FFmpeg backend (LGPL-2.1+)
upstream_notes.lib*.dll, *.dll: Remaining upstream libraries pulled in by the dependency walk (zlib, brotli, freetype, harfbuzz, pcre2, libpng, zstd and similar). The catch-all is safe because it only marks a file as UPSTREAM: an upstream file that claims ProductName=Lightning still fails, and only the explicit lightning_owned list is ever signed.
